# Intake Brief: help screen and improved help line (WL-0MTV97GV20088CS7)

## Problem statement

The Herdr work-item selection list footer advertises only a small, mixed-signal
subset of the available keyboard shortcuts — including the low-value
`d:downtime toggle` and the mouse-tracking hint `alt+m mouse on` — while offering
no discoverable reference for the full command set or for the meaning of the
icons rendered on each row. Users cannot discover what keys are available or
what the glyphs mean without reading the source.

## Users

Herdr producers and agents who navigate work items in the pane-based selection
list and rely on the footer and on-screen glyphs to operate the tool.

**User stories:**

- As a Herdr user, I want a single `?` shortcut that opens a help screen, so I
  can discover every available command without reading the source.
- As a Herdr user, I want the help screen to explain every icon shown in the
  list, so I can interpret the status, stage, priority, risk, effort, audit and
  agent glyphs at a glance.
- As a Herdr user, I want the footer help line to advertise the help screen
  rather than rarely-used toggles, so the most useful discovery path is always
  visible.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Footer help line updated** — In the selection list footer, the
   `d:downtime toggle` entry is no longer advertised and `?: Help` is shown
   instead. The `d` key binding itself remains functional (only its inline
   advertisement is removed).
2. **Mouse hint removed from footer** — The `alt+m mouse on` / `alt+m mouse off`
   footer hint is removed. The `Alt+m` mouse-tracking toggle itself remains
   functional and is documented in the help screen.
3. **Help screen opens on `?`** — Pressing `?` in the selection list opens a
   dedicated help screen (full-pane overlay). Pressing `?`, `Esc`, or `q`
   dismisses it and returns to the list with no state mutation (selection,
   filters, and navigation stack unchanged).
4. **Help screen lists all commands** — The help screen enumerates every
   registered shortcut available in the selection list, grouped by chord
   leader, showing the chord key(s), label and a short description. The list is
   derived from the live `ShortcutRegistry` so future shortcut additions appear
   automatically.
5. **Help screen identifies all icons** — The help screen includes an icon
   legend that identifies every glyph rendered in work-item rows (at minimum:
   status, stage, priority, epic, risk, effort, audit, producer-review, agent
   state and child-coverage icons), each with a short meaning.
6. **Graceful on small panes** — The help screen renders within the pane height
   without overflowing the `rows - 1` render budget (scroll or truncate when
   content exceeds the viewport; the dismiss keys remain discoverable).
7. **Tests** — New/updated tests verify: (a) the footer shows `?: Help` and no
   longer shows `d:downtime toggle` or `alt+m mouse on/off`; (b) the help
   screen renders the registered commands and the icon legend; (c) `?` toggles
   the help screen on and off without mutating list state.
8. **Documentation** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, `docs/TUI.md`, the icon legend in
   `docs/icons-design.md` (if the on-screen legend wording is authoritative) and
   any relevant README entries.
9. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Must not break existing chord handling: `?` must not conflict with any
  registered shortcut chord or navigation key.
- Backward compatibility: all existing shortcut key bindings (including `d` and
  `Alt+m`) continue to function unchanged; only their footer advertisement
  changes.
- The help screen is display-only/read-only — it must not dispatch commands, spawn
  panes, or mutate the worklog.
- Icon legend content must be derived from the single source of truth
  (`@worklog/shared/icons`) rather than a hand-maintained duplicate list, so it
  cannot drift.
- Must respect the existing `showHelpText` gate (when help text is disabled, the
  help screen and its footer hint are not offered).

## Existing state

- **Footer hint assembly** — `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` composes the
  footer from `formatFooterShortcutHints()` (single-key entries render as
  `key:label`) plus an explicit mouse-tracking hint appended at render time
  (`dynamicHints` around the "Mouse-tracking toggle hint
  (WL-0MT0AP2LR000JFWN)" block). The `d` entry comes from
  `src/shortcuts.json` (`chord: ["d"]`, `label: "downtime toggle"`).
- **View modes** — `ViewMode = 'list' | 'detail' | 'filter' | 'form'`
  (`worklist.ts`). `renderWorklist()` branches on mode; `filter` mode shows a
  simple full-pane prompt — the closest existing precedent for a full-pane help
  overlay.
- **Key handling** — `keyToAction()` maps navigation keys; single-key shortcut
  resolution and chord handling happen in the main key loop. No `?` handling
  exists today.
- **Icons** — all row glyphs come from `@worklog/shared/icons`
  (`statusIcon`, `stageIcon`, `priorityIcon`, `epicIcon`, `riskIcon`,
  `effortIcon`, `auditIcon`, `needsProducerReviewIcon`, `agentStatusIcon`,
  `getIconPrefixParts`/`isCoveredByParent`). `docs/icons-design.md` documents the
  icon set and accessible labels.
- **Shortcut registry** — `ShortcutRegistry.getChordEntries()` /
  `getEntriesForStage()` expose all valid entries with `chord`, `label` and
  `description`, gated by code-freeze and issue-type.

## Desired change

1. **Footer (`formatFooterShortcutHints` / render-time composition):**
   - Exclude the `d:downtime toggle` single-key entry from the footer hint (or
     suppress its advertisement while keeping the binding).
   - Prepend/insert a literal `?: Help` hint.
   - Remove the `alt+m mouse on/off` suffix block.

2. **New help mode:** add `'help'` to `ViewMode`; render a full-pane help
   overlay in `renderWorklist()` with two sections — **Commands** (grouped by
   leader, `chord → label — description`) and **Icons** (glyph → meaning) —
   respecting the pane height budget.

3. **Key binding:** in list mode, `?` toggles the help mode on; inside help
   mode, `?`, `Esc` and `q` return to the previous mode (record the
   pre-help mode, mirroring the existing `preFormMode` pattern).

4. **Tests:** extend `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` (and/or a focused
   `worklist-help.test.ts`) for the footer and help-screen behaviour.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `ViewMode`, `formatFooterShortcutHints()`,
  footer composition (mouse-hint block), `renderWorklist()` help overlay, key
  handling (`?`), help-content builder.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` — `ShortcutRegistry` used to enumerate
  commands for the help screen (read-only; no signature change expected).
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — icon definitions used to build the legend
  (read-only; source of truth).
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — shortcut definitions; no new entry
  required if `?` is a reserved key, but a `?` entry may be added for
  discoverability.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` (and/or new
  `packages/herdr/src/worklist-help.test.ts`) — footer and help-screen tests.
- `docs/TUI.md` — document the `?` help screen and updated footer.
- `docs/icons-design.md` — icon legend reference (update if wording is
  authoritative).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — shortcut/help summary if present.

## Related work

- **WL-0MQDR5HZC006JWOK** — "Show available shortcut keys in browse list help
  text" (completed). Introduced the dynamic shortcut hint line this work
  extends.
- **WL-0MRMG8P2X004V6YC** — "help line for chord commands too verbose"
  (completed). Collapsed/trimmed chord hints in the same footer.
- **WL-0MQDUOK9K002QHJU** — "Stage-based shortcut condition filters" (completed).
  Added stage-aware shortcut filtering used when enumerating help entries.
- **WL-0MT0AP2LR000JFWN** — mouse-tracking toggle (`Alt+m`) whose footer hint
  this work removes.
- **WL-0MSZ4NSOE007AQEF** — `/downtime toggle` command backing the `d` shortcut.
- **WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ** — "Herdr worklist: mouse and touch support in the
  selection list" (completed). Directly related: owns the mouse-tracking
  behaviour whose `Alt+m` footer hint this work removes.
- **WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94** — heading/display-row model used by the renderer.
- **WL-0MTV979LK005YB1B** — footer wrap guard (relevant to keeping the help
  overlay within the render budget).

None of these are duplicates or blockers — they provide historical context for
the footer, chord and renderer subsystems.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MTD0IVNN003WCOB** – Warn in wl export/import --help that export dumps the whole DB and import REPLACEs it (completed)
- **WL-0MUN4ARHA001SN40** – Research classic enemies from the arcade games of old (open)
- **WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ** – Herdr worklist: mouse and touch support in the selection list (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: add, alt, commands, downtime, help (+13 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: add, alt, commands, downtime, help (+13 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: add, alt, downtime, help, icons (+10 more)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — `d` binding retained:** "replace `d:downtime toggle` with
  `?: Help`" is interpreted as replacing the footer *advertisement* only; the
  `d` key continues to toggle downtime and is documented in the help screen.
- **Assumption — `Alt+m` retained:** the mouse-tracking toggle remains
  functional; only its footer advertisement is removed (documented in the help
  screen).
- **Assumption — list view scope:** the help screen is offered in the selection
  list. Detail-view command help is out of scope unless trivially reachable.
- **Risk — key conflict:** `?` must not collide with a registered chord or
  navigation key; verify against `shortcuts.json` and `keyToAction()`.
- **Risk — icon-legend drift:** hard-coding the legend duplicates the icon
  source of truth. Mitigate by deriving rows from `@worklog/shared/icons` where
  practical, or add a test asserting every legend glyph matches the exported
  icon.
- **Scope-creep risk:** a full command *reference* (rendering help text for
  detail/form modes) is out of scope; record such follow-ups as linked work
  items rather than expanding this one.
- **Small-pane risk:** the combined commands + icons content can exceed short
  panes; require truncation/scroll so the footer stays one row and the render
  invariant holds.
- **Performance risk:** negligible — help content is computed only when the
  help screen is opened.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were asked — the work-item description and code analysis
provided sufficient detail. Assumptions above were applied where the seed
context was ambiguous and are recorded for producer review.

# Herdr selection list: base the in-progress marker on work-item tab existence

## Problem statement

The "in progress" marker shown in the Herdr selection list is unreliable: it is
derived from the worklog `in-progress` status, which is maintained by the
hydrator — a self-healing loop that decides whether a claimed item is genuinely
being worked on by matching the item ID against live **pane titles**
(`packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts`). That pane-title matching predates the
one-tab-per-work-item convention: every interactive/downtime dispatch now places
its agent pane in a tab labelled with the **exact work-item ID**
(`getItemTabAnchor` / `findTabByLabel` in `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts`).
Panes can be re-parented, renamed, truncated or multi-pane per tab, so pane-title
matching produces false negatives (→ wrong demotion, marker disappears while work
continues) and is needlessly complex.

## Users

- Herdr operator selecting the next work item from the selection list.
- Downtime dispatcher / plugin panes that rely on the hydrator to release stale
  `in-progress` claims so the item re-enters the dispatchable pool.

Example user stories:

- As a Herdr operator, I want the selection list's in-progress marker to reflect
  reality — an item is "being worked on" iff a tab named after its work-item ID
  exists in my workspace — so I can trust the list without opening tabs.
- As a dispatched agent, I want my claimed item left `in-progress` for as long as
  my work-item tab is open, so my claim is never released underneath me.
- As an operator, I want a stale claim (no work-item tab) released automatically
  and periodically so abandoned items return to the dispatchable pool.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An item is treated as actively worked **iff** a tab in the current workspace (`HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, or `herdr tab list --workspace <id>`) has a label **equal to** the work-item ID; a tab label that merely *contains* the ID does not count, and a pane title containing the ID no longer counts on its own. Verified by unit tests over a pure tab-matching helper.
- [ ] The hydrator's active detection is switched from `herdr pane list` + pane-title ID extraction to `herdr tab list --workspace <id>` + exact tab label match; the pane-matching seam/types (`HydratorPane`, `listActivePanes`, `collectPaneWorkItemIds`, `isActivePaneMatch`) are replaced by tab equivalents. Verified by code review + updated `hydrator.test.ts` (no `pane list` spawn asserted).
- [ ] Demotion rules are unchanged: a non-active item at stage `in_review` → `completed`/`in_review`; a non-active item with an active outbound blocker → `blocked`; otherwise → `open` (stage repaired to a compatible value). An item with a matching tab is never demoted. Verified by unit tests.
- [ ] The signal is refreshed periodically from the selection list: the existing 30 s hydrate task (`HYDRATOR_INTERVAL_MS`) and the hidden→visible focus-resume hook both re-evaluate tab existence, so a closed work-item tab clears the marker within one cadence and an opened tab keeps it. Verified by existing scheduler/visibility tests plus a tab-based hydration test.
- [ ] Fail-open preserved: an unavailable/unparseable `herdr tab list` aborts the cycle without demoting, and tabs outside the current workspace never mark an item active. Verified by unit tests.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs site entries (notably the hydrator module header, `pane-title.ts` rationale comment and `herdr-agent-state-protocol.md` if it references pane-title matching).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Do not change the worklog status/stage vocabulary or the demotion outcome rules.
- Keep the bounded/responsive hydrator contract (per-step timeout, per-tick cap,
  stdio isolation, fail-open) unchanged; only the "which items are active" lookup
  changes.
- Reuse the existing tab listing/parsing (`listTabsInWorkspace`,
  `parseTabListOutput`, `findTabByLabel`) rather than adding a second parser.
- Retain exports still used elsewhere: `extractWorkItemIdsFromText`
  (`ship-guard.ts`) and `isActiveBlocker` (`stalled-work.ts`).
- No CLI or socket API change; `herdr tab list` is already used by the plugin.
- Write in UK English; follow the project's test/build conventions.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — fetches `wl list --status in-progress`,
  fetches `herdr pane list [--workspace <id>]`, collects work-item IDs from pane
  labels (`WORK_ITEM_ID_REGEX` over `pane.label`), and demotes items with no
  matching pane. Exposes pure helpers (`collectPaneWorkItemIds`,
  `isActivePaneMatch`, `decideDemotion`, `compatibleStage`, `isActiveBlocker`).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — creates the hydrator runner with
  `workspaceId: process.env.HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, runs it every 30 s (`hydrate`
  task) and on hidden→visible focus-resume. The selection list's in-progress
  marker (`statusIcon(item.status)`) and Group N ordering (`status ===
  'in-progress'`) are driven by the worklog status this loop maintains.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts` — already lists/creates tabs labelled
  with the exact item ID: `listTabsInWorkspace`, `parseTabListOutput`,
  `findTabByLabel`, `getItemTabAnchor`.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-title.ts` — truncation helper exists specifically so
  the ID survives in pane titles for the hydrator; this rationale becomes obsolete
  for matching (the helper may remain for human-readable titles).

## Desired change

Replace the hydrator's pane-title-based "is this item active" signal with a
tab-label-based one:

1. Add a pure helper that, given the tabs of the current workspace, returns the
   set of work-item IDs whose tab label matches exactly (e.g.
   `collectTabWorkItemIds(tabs)` / `hasItemTab(itemId, tabs)`).
2. Change `HydratorDeps.listActivePanes` → `listTabs(workspaceId)` backed by
   `herdr tab list --workspace <id>` (reusing the shared parser), and update
   `runHydrationOnce` to use tab membership.
3. Keep `decideDemotion`, `compatibleStage`, `isActiveBlocker`,
   `extractWorkItemIdsFromText` and the bounded-run machinery intact.
4. Update tests and the module/doc comments to describe tab-based detection.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — replace pane matching with exact tab-label matching; rename seam/types/helpers.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts` — reuse/export `listTabsInWorkspace` / `parseTabListOutput` / `findTabByLabel` for the hydrator's tab lookup.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — hydrator wiring (workspace id, cadence, focus-resume); update comments if needed.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts` — rewrite active-pane cases as active-tab cases; add exact-match, workspace-scope and fail-open cases.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.fixtures.ts` — replace `makeWorstCasePanes` with tab fixtures and update the exec router to answer `tab list`.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator-responsiveness.test.ts` — update to the tab-based deps.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-title.ts` — adjust/retire the "hydrator matches pane titles" rationale comment.
- `packages/herdr/shared/herdr-agent-state-protocol.md` — update if it documents pane-title matching for the hydrator.

## Related work

- WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI — Herdr hydrator: rescue `in_progress` work items with no active pane (parent of the pane-matching design).
- WL-0MTF5WO2Q008B8US — Hydrator: demote stale `in_progress` items (child, currently blocked).
- WL-0MUY1CXSV008F8TZ / WL-0MUY1CYCB003DTKO / WL-0MUY1CYV6008BQWX — bounded/isolated hydrate steps (contract to preserve).
- WL-0MUKXFWLD006A8XI / WL-0MUYI3JAO002BTNL — item-ID tab anchor and interactive dispatch wiring (the tab-per-item convention this builds on).
- WL-0MUY1CS9E006ZLS0 — re-based Herdr in-progress UI behaviour on `status` (the marker this work makes reliable).
- WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9 — per-row agent-status icon (separate, richer herdr agent-reporting signal; out of scope here).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MLX5OADB1TECIZV** – Testing: automation - create work item (completed)
- **WL-0MM0DTK1B1Z0VMIB** – wl list --stage in_review returns nothing while --json shows content (completed)
- **WL-0MT0AP2LR000JFWN** – Herdr: re-enable terminal drag-select while keeping mouse support (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: base, carries, detection, existence, herdr (+17 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: base, carries, detection, existence, herdr (+17 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: base, carries, detection, herdr, iff (+15 more)

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption (scope):** "the logic for discovering when an item is being worked
  on" is the hydrator's active detection; the selection-list in-progress marker
  follows from the status the hydrator maintains. The agent-status icon
  (`AgentTracker`, herdr `agent list`) is a distinct feature and is not changed.
- **Assumption:** tabs are labelled with the exact work-item ID
  (`getItemTabAnchor` / `findTabByLabel` convention), so exact label equality is
  the correct match; substring matching is rejected to avoid false positives.
- **Assumption:** `herdr tab list` returns `result.tabs[].label` (and `tab_id`),
  as parsed by `parseTabListOutput`; no new herdr capability is required.
- **Risk:** legacy tabs created before the item-ID convention (or hand-created
  tabs) may not be labelled with the ID, so an item could be demoted while a
  legacy pane is still active. Mitigation: the item-ID tab convention is now the
  only dispatch path; document the change.
- **Risk:** a tab may outlive its agent (kept open after the agent finishes),
  leaving an item `in-progress`. This matches the requested rule (tab = worked
  on); operators close the tab to release the item.
- **Scope-creep risk:** sharing the signal with `AgentTracker` or the agent-status
  icon. Record any such opportunity as a linked follow-up work item, not in scope
  here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which 'logic for discovering when an item is being worked on' should switch
  to tab existence: the hydrator's stale-claim detection, or a new
  display-layer marker?" — **Assumed answer** (Map, from the intake seed): the
  hydrator's stale-claim detection, whose status output drives the selection-list
  in-progress marker. Evidence: `hydrator.ts` is the only discovery logic
  (pane-title matching predating per-item tabs); the worklist runs it every 30 s
  and on focus-resume. Source: interactive intake request; recorded as an
  assumption for producer confirmation at review.
- Q: "Does tab 'matching the work item ID' mean exact label equality or
  contains?" — **Assumed answer** (Map): exact equality, consistent with
  `findTabByLabel` ("never a substring/prefix match") and `getItemTabAnchor`
  (tab labelled exactly the item ID). Source: repo inspection.
- Q: "Should a matching tab require a live pane inside it?" — **Assumed answer**
  (Map): no — tab existence is the signal, per the seed request ("If there is a
  tab ... then it is being worked on"). Source: interactive intake request.

## Plan (decomposition)

Planned 2026-10-10. Three child work items, created in dependency order:

1. **WL-0MV24RM9I0051GEF** — Hydrator: switch active detection to exact tab-label
   matching (core + test migration). Vertical slice: `hydrator.ts` types, pure
   helpers, orchestration and production wiring, plus the structural test/fixture
   migration needed to keep the package green.
2. **WL-0MV24T2VJ007Q49J** — Verification: tab-matching edge cases (exact match,
   substring rejection, workspace scoping, fail-open, no pane-list spawn) plus
   the responsiveness-suite migration. Depends on the core item.
3. **WL-0MV25EE4E0028KDI** — Docs: hydrator module header, `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md`,
   `packages/herdr/README.md` and the `pane-title.ts` rationale comment. Depends on
   the core item.

Test-first: the core item follows TDD (tab-matching tests written/extended before
the implementation); the verification item adds the exhaustive behavioural
coverage demanded by this item's ACs.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-10 — Created the three child items above and wired the dependency
  edges (verification → core; docs → core).
- 2026-10-10 — Reformatted the multi-line acceptance-criteria bullets into
  single-line bullets so automated AC-coverage extraction works (no intent
  change; the prior line wrapping truncated every AC to its first line).

# Intake Brief: Herdr downtime audit claim leaves item in-progress/in_review; failed audit strands review-queue items

## Problem statement

The herdr downtime dispatcher's audit-tier pre-dispatch CAS claim flips a `completed`/`in_review` item's status to `in_progress` while leaving the stage at `in_review`, creating a hybrid state that the audit runner's own inlined `_STATUS_STAGE_COMPAT` table rejects. When the audit then fails (Phase-2 timeout, infra failure), the runner's failure-restore coerces the hybrid to `in-progress`/`plan_complete`, stranding the item one step down — off the review queue, out of the audit tier's selection, and out of the release gate's visibility.

## Users

- **Operator** (runs herdr downtime dispatch): wants audit auto-dispatch to be transparent — no item should silently change state as a side effect of being audited.
- **Producer/reviewer**: wants every `in_review` item to stay on the review queue (observable via `completed`/`in_review`) until a genuine audit verdict or manual action moves it, so infra failures never invisibly remove work from review.
- **Auto-dispatched audit agent** (`/skill:audit <id>`): wants pre-flight guard and pre-audit state capture to see the true pre-claim state (`completed`/`in_review`), not the dispatcher's claim artifact.

User stories:
- As an operator, when herdr auto-dispatches an audit of a `completed`/`in_review` item and the audit fails, the item must remain `completed`/`in_review` so a re-run or manual review can still proceed.
- As a producer, I want no failed audit to ever strand an item at `in-progress`/`plan_complete`, invisible to the review queue and the audit tier.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When the herdr audit tier dispatches an audit of a `completed`/`in_review` item, the item's observable state (via `wl show`) never becomes `in-progress`/`in_review` as a dispatch artifact — the claim is status- and stage-neutral (or restores the pre-claim state as the single visible state while the audit runs only where the runner itself manages the lifecycle).

- After a failed/interrupted herdr-dispatched audit of a `completed`/`in_review` item (Phase-2 timeout, infra failure, SIGKILL, pane kill), the item is verified back at `completed`/`in_review` via `wl show` readback — never `in-progress`/`plan_complete`, and never left `in_progress`.

- The audit runner's failure-restore and abort-recovery (SIGKILL state-file) paths restore `completed`/`in_review` for review-queue items, including when the captured pre-audit state is the herdr claim hybrid — no coercion to `plan_complete`. Covered by unit + integration tests.

- Double-dispatch protection (RCA WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT design point 1: exactly one concurrent pane wins the claim) is preserved; the alternative claim mechanism has its own race-safety test.

- The existing `in-progress`/`in_review` transitional exception in the wl validator (`src/status-stage-validation.ts`) is retained or tightened only in step with the chosen fix (never removed while herdr can still create the hybrid); regression tests for the validator remain green.

- **Testing/validation criterion:** all of the above are covered by meaningful tests (unit + an integration-style dispatch→failed-audit→restore scenario); the full project test suite passes with the changes.

- **Documentation criterion:** all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes — `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `AGENTS.md` (claim pattern), and any relevant skill docs (`/skill:audit` README note on CAS claims).

- **Suite criterion:** full project test suite must pass with the new changes (ContextHub `tests/` + `packages/herdr`); cross-repo audit-runner tests in the owning project where the fix lands.

## Constraints

- **Repo boundary (decided 2026-10-14):** `audit_runner.py` lives in the shared skills install sourced from the SorraAgents repo (`skill/audit`), not this repo. Changes there happen via that repo's own work items (SA work item), linked from here as `Blocked-by`. This bug is the tracking/verification item.
- The dispatch-failure rollback path (`rollbackClaimWorkItem`) already restores `completed`/`in_review` for audit (fetcher.ts `rollbackClaimWorkItem`); it must keep working and be covered.
- `needsProducerReview` removal and the assignee-based scheduling hold are out of scope for the *immediate* bug fix — they belong to epic WL-0MV82CHGQ000HAZZ (Option A follow-on). This item must not depend on that epic landing.
- Keep the fix surgical: no behaviour change to the other tiers' claims (they legitimately claim `open` items as in_progress) or to the review-queue depth gate.

# Epic: Option A — status-neutral assignee CAS claim for the audit tier + remove `needsProducerReview`

## Problem statement

When the herdr downtime worker auto-dispatches an audit of a completed/in_review item, its CAS claim flips `status` to `in_progress` while leaving the stage at `in_review`, creating a hybrid `in-progress`/`in_review` pair that the audit runner's failure-restore path cannot represent — so a failed audit (Phase 2 timeout, infra failure, killed pane) coerces the item to `in-progress`/`plan_complete`, stranding it off the review queue (root cause: WL-0MV7W77AY005MGBL). Separately, `needsProducerReview` has grown into a magic DB flag whose two roles — blocking auto-dispatch and gating the ship release — need to be re-homed onto the assignee field so the flag and its whole surface (`wl reviewed`, CLI/API filters, herdr icon/logic, audit runner, ship gate) can be removed.

## Users

- **Operator** running herdr downtime dispatch. Story: "When an auto-dispatched audit of a completed/in_review item fails, I want the item to stay completed/in_review — on the review queue and re-selectable — so broken audits never strand work in in-progress/plan_complete."
- **Producer** reviewing work. Story: "I want an explicit, per-item way to pause automatic scheduling (assign the item to me) that does not rely on a magic DB flag, and I want a release gate that still stops me from shipping unreviewed work."
- **Agent tier / pane** competing for the same item. Story: "Exactly one concurrent claim must win, even when the claim does not change status."

## Approach (Option A, per root cause fix-options)

Make the audit-tier claim **status-neutral**: the claim's CAS becomes the **assignee** instead of `status`. Add `--if-assignee <value>` to `wl update` (atomic `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` CAS, same machinery as `updateIfMatches`), then the audit-tier claim writes:

```
wl update <id> --assignee <agent> --if-status completed --if-stage in_review --if-assignee ""
```

The item stays completed/in_review throughout — no hybrid state is ever created, so the audit runner's pre-audit capture and failure-restore are correct (no `_STATUS_STAGE_COMPAT` coercion to plan_complete). Exactly one pane still wins (CAS on the guarded fields), preserving the WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT RC-1 single-claim guarantee.

Remove `needsProducerReview` from the database and re-home its two roles onto the assignee field:
- **Scheduling hold:** assign to the producer ⇒ no tier claims it ⇒ no auto-dispatch.
- **Release gate:** an item assigned to the producer means "the producer owns it"; `check-final-validation.js` blocks release until such items have been reviewed (audit verdict 'Ready to close: Yes').

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `wl update` supports `--if-assignee` CAS (atomic, single-winner; unit + integration tests).
- [ ] Audit-tier claim is status-neutral: item stays completed/in_review through dispatch and failed-audit restore (`wl show` after simulated failure shows completed/in_review).
- [ ] Regression test: herdr dispatch claim → simulated audit Phase-2 failure → item back at completed/in_review, re-selectable (no in-progress/plan_complete, no needsProducerReview-column dependency).
- [ ] Failed dispatch (marker-write-failed / spawn-failed) clears assignee and leaves item re-selectable.
- [ ] Success path clears assignee; legacy residue cleared by a one-time migration/script; audit re-runs still dispatch.
- [ ] Assign item to producer ⇒ no tier auto-dispatches it (claims fail stale at every tier) — the scheduling hold works.
- [ ] `needsProducerReview` column removed from DB; `wl reviewed` and all `--needs-producer-review` CLI/API options removed; no references left in src/, packages/, skill/, .pi/skills/.
- [ ] Ship release gate re-homed onto the assignee hold without weakening release safety (check-final-validation.js updated + tested).
- [ ] Sync regression guard behaviour for assignee documented/decided and tested cross-root.
- [ ] Full test suite passes; CLI.md / docs updated; AGENTS.md claim pattern updated.

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo skill boundary:** `audit_runner.py`, `status_lifecycle.py`, and the ship gate scripts (`check-final-validation.js`, `check-audit-gate.js`, `run-release.js`) live in the **SorraAgents** skill tree (`~/.pi/agent/skills` → `SorraAgents/skill`). AGENTS.md forbids editing `skill/` dirs without explicit instruction; changes there must be tracked as SA work items linked from here (see bug intake question 2 — repo boundary, still awaiting producer answer).
- **No hybrid status/stage write:** the new claim path must never produce `in-progress`/`in_review`; the old dual-set claim is the bug's source.
- **Race safety preserved:** the `--if-assignee ""` guard is the exclusive token; rollback must be similarly guarded (`--if-assignee <agent>`) so only this claim's state is reverted.
- **Assignee residue is a live problem:** 698 completed items and 7 in_review items already carry `assignee=Map` (P1); the legacy-cleanup is table-stakes or the queue ossifies.
- **Sync regression guard:** `assignee` is merge-participating and `'Map' → ''` is refused as a regression on other roots unless the guard is changed or `--accept-regressions` used (P3).
- **Migration history preserved:** the add-migration (20260210-add-needsProducerReview) stays for history; a new drop-migration removes the column.
- **Docs/conventions:** AGENTS.md claim pattern, herdr README downtime-dispatcher docs, docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md, CLI.md, icons-design.md, CHANGELOG updated.
- **UK English, Markdown descriptions, wl is source of truth** per project rules.
- **Push only to `dev`** per push policy.

## Existing state

- `wl update` supports `--if-status` / `--if-stage` CAS (used by `claimWorkItem` in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`, which flips `--status in_progress --assignee <agent>`); no `--if-assignee` field exists yet.
- `claimWorkItem` (fetcher.ts:1197) and `rollbackClaimWorkItem` (fetcher.ts:1268) implement the dispatch claim/rollback; `downtime-worker.ts` (`dispatchClaimedTier`, `rollbackClaimForFailure`, `classifyItemForDispatch`, all `select*` functions) consumes them.
- `needsProducerReview` is stored in the DB (column, migration 20260210-add-needsProducerReview), exposed via `wl reviewed` (src/commands/reviewed.ts), `wl update --needs-producer-review`, `wl list/search/next` filters, api.ts query param, cli-types, persistent-store schema/jsonl/sync.
- The audit runner (SorraAgents `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`) sets `--needs-producer-review yes` on 'yes' verdicts and never clears `--assignee ""` (P1). Its failure-restore path has an inlined `_STATUS_STAGE_COMPAT` that coerces `in_review → plan_complete`.
- The ship release gate (`skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js`) blocks release on `needsProducerReview === true` items.
- `interview.ts` explains/clears the flag (P5); github.js `--add-assignee` and delegate-helper write `assignee=@github-copilot` (P6).

## Desired change

- Add `--if-assignee` CAS to `wl update` (atomic single-winner).
- herdr audit-tier claim becomes status-neutral (assignee CAS against `""`); dispatch rollback clears assignee guarded on `--if-assignee <agent>`; audit runner clears assignee on every terminal verdict path (success 'yes', failure restore, verdict 'no').
- Define the scheduling-hold convention: non-empty assignee = item intentionally held from auto-dispatch (assign → producer ⇒ hold). All skills clear assignee on session end (status_lifecycle failure-exit already does; intake/delegate/triage reviewed).
- One-time legacy cleanup of assignee residue (698+ items).
- Drop `needsProducerReview` everywhere: migration, persistent-store/sync/jsonl, CLI/API (`wl reviewed`, filters, query params, cli-types), herdr (grouping, icons, pane-lifecycle, pane-close*, stalled-work, settings, fetcher, downtime-worker select*/classify), theme.ts, interview.ts, audit runner ('yes' verdict path), ship check-final-validation.js (re-homed onto assignee hold), docs.
- Sync regression guard handled per open question Q1.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/update.ts` — add `--if-assignee` CAS (normalizeActionArgs + update path)
- `src/persistent-store.ts` / `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` / `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `updateIfMatches`/CAS field surface, column removal, schema/CRUD
- `src/sync.ts` — merge-participating/regression-guard behaviour for `assignee` (Q1)
- `src/commands/reviewed.ts` — remove/repurpose the command
- `src/commands/list.ts`, `src/commands/search.ts`, `src/commands/next.ts`, `src/commands/create.ts`, `src/api.ts`, `src/cli-types.ts` — remove `--needs-producer-review` options/param
- `src/commands/grouping.ts`, `src/commands/helpers.ts`, `src/theme.ts` — producer-review icon/flags
- `src/commands/interview.ts` — flag explain/clear flow (replace or update)
- `src/migrations/index.ts` — drop-column migration
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — status-neutral `claimWorkItem` + guarded `rollbackClaimWorkItem` (+ `--if-assignee`)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — dispatch claim/rollback/select*/classifyItemForDispatch (filtering moves to assignee-based)
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`, `pane-close-herdr.ts`, pane-lifecycle/stalled-work/settings — `needsProducerReview` icon/logic removal
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (SorraAgents) — clear assignee on terminal verdicts; 'yes' verdict producer-hold
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` (SorraAgents) — assignee-clear conventions (already on failure)
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js` (SorraAgents) — release gate re-homed onto assignee hold (+ `check-audit-gate.js`, `run-release.js`)
- Tests: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker*.test.ts`, `tests/cli/*`, `tests/unit/*`, migration tests
- Docs: `AGENTS.md` (both repos), `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md`, `CLI.md`, `docs/icons-design.md`

## Related work

- WL-0MV7W77AY005MGBL — root cause bug (depends-on blocker of this epic; its intake interview on fix approach + repo boundary is awaiting producer answers)
- WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT — RCA: downtime dispatcher re-dispatches same item (CAS claim design point 1; RC-1 single-claim guarantee this epic must preserve)
- WL-0MTYL7DX9000MZOH — downtime dispatcher hard-strikes on retired 'in_progress' stage (retired-stage `migrateStage` claim path in fetcher.ts)
- WL-0MTQ14W7L003II5A — cross-root coordination offers (per-call `--worklog-dir` claim targeting; P3 cross-root concern)
- WL-0MSN6ZCTN0027U2R — herdr: flipping needsProducerReview must not make a valid audit stale
- WL-0MU72WJ8C0005GIE — herdr dispatcher ignores needsProducerReview on live dispatch path
- WL-0MTIAL65N004T22F — downtime dispatcher excludes items needing producer review from selection
- WL-0MT3FM8VA005XBHE — critical items always progress first (dispatch ordering)
- WL-0MT32F908002YFFA — recover items stranded by marker-write-failed / spawn-failed
- WL-0MT8KSTOE00871E7 — herdr audit tier re-checks for fresh audit after selection
- WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN — conditional claim + plan/intake marker exclusion
- SA side (SorraAgents): audit runner items, ship gate items (linked during planning)

## Out of scope

- Option B (audit_runner `_STATUS_STAGE_COMPAT` addition) — keep as fallback if Option A is blocked; the bug's intake recommends a staged interim audit-runner fix (Option B as a small SA-side item first), which is tracked on the root-cause bug, not here.
- Changing the implement/plan/intake tiers' status flip (they are legitimately in_progress while worked).

## Risks & assumptions

- **R1 — Assignee-hold convention breaks existing flows.** Any skill that leaves a non-empty assignee (intake, implement, triage, delegate `@github-copilot`) silently suppresses future auto-dispatch. Mitigation: audit every assignee writer, clear on session end (status_lifecycle failure-exit already does), document in AGENTS.md, and add a test that a cleared claim re-enables dispatch.
- **R2 — Legacy residue cleanup could strand live items.** The one-time cleanup of 698 completed + 7 in_review assigned items must run after the code change ships, be idempotent, and scope to audit-hold residue only (not e.g. in-flight implement claims).
- **R3 — Release-gate weakening.** Re-homing the ship gate onto the assignee hold must not make unreviewed items shippable. Mitigation: gate checks producer-assigned items for a passing audit ('Ready to close: Yes') before closeWorkItemsAfterRelease.
- **R4 — Cross-repo coordination.** Skill-side changes (audit_runner, status_lifecycle, ship gate) live in SorraAgents; if they are not tracked/implemented via SA work items, the epic's AC "no references left" cannot be met. Assumed: SA items are created during planning (pending the bug's repo-boundary answer).
- **R5 — Sync regression guard fights assignee clearing** (P3) and **R6 — `--if-assignee` needs full CAS semantics** (atomic `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, mirrors `--if-status`/`--if-stage`; introduced in `wl update` only, not other commands) — both captured in ACs (9 and 1).

## Open questions (Appendix)

- Q1 (sync regression guard, P3): (a) treat `assignee` as a normal non-regression-guarded merge field so `''` clears propagate cross-root, or (b) accept `assignee` as an owned reconciliation field and document the cross-root rule? **Recommended: (a)** — the status-neutral claim's whole point is that the cleared assignee must propagate so the item is re-selectable everywhere; a regression-guarded assignee resurrects claims across panes/roots and would need `--accept-regressions` noise on every sync. **ACCEPTED — option (a), implemented and tested in WL-0MV85WBZ2004VDUQ (C3).** `assignee` is removed from the regression-guard merge-participating fields in `src/sync.ts` and its empty value is treated as meaningful intent (`isEmptyMeaningfulField`), so a newer remote `''` clears a local non-empty assignee and propagates cross-root without `--accept-regressions` (last-writer-wins by `updatedAt`; deterministic tie-break at equal timestamps). Status/stage/priority remain guarded. Coverage: `tests/cli/sync-assignee-clear.test.ts` (two roots, real `wl sync`) and unit tests in `tests/sync-regression-guard.test.ts`.
- Q2 (producer-hold assignee value, P5/P7): what literal value marks the producer hold (e.g. operator identity `rog`, a reserved `producer` sentinel, or `@github-copilot`-style)? **Recommended: a reserved well-known value equal to the producer's wl identity used by the release gate** so the hold is self-describing; exact value to be confirmed with the producer. **OPEN QUESTION — record the operator's identity during planning.**
- Q3 (dependency direction): this epic currently holds `depends-on` → WL-0MV7W77AY005MGBL (the root-cause bug it resolves), leaving it `blocked`. Confirm this is intentional sequencing (bug root-cause decided first) vs. the epic superseding the bug. **Recommended: keep depends-on on the root cause until its intake decision lands, then have the epic's completion close the bug as fixed-by (recorded as related work; direction reviewed at planning).** **OPEN QUESTION — traceability reviewed during planning.**

*Source: repository inspection (fetcher.ts, downtime-worker.ts, sync.ts, reviewed.ts, interview.ts, migrations, SorraAgents skill tree), bug intake records, and work-item history. No interactive interview conducted — herdr-dispatched session; seed context was exhaustive.*

# Herdr selection list: `Blocked By` metadata line flickers endlessly on blocked items (WL-0MV8Q5X8U004KKAP)

**Headline:** The Herdr metadata panel has two live render states for a blocked item (async `Blocked By` lookup pending → line absent; resolved → line present), and `doRefresh()` clears the per-item blocker cache on *every* list refresh, so frequent refresh triggers (DB-change watch, auto-sync counter bumps, `wl next` re-sorts) re-flip the panel between the two states endlessly. Fix: make the resolved state survive refreshes and invalidate only when the item's dependency edges can actually change.

## Problem statement

In the Herdr work-item selection list, selecting a dependency-blocked item makes the metadata panel's `Blocked By` line appear for a moment, then disappear for a moment, then reappear — repeating endlessly. Selecting a blocked item is therefore visually noisy and leaves the "what is this blocked on?" answer (added by WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8) unreliable at a glance.

## RCA (root cause analysis)

There are two distinct render states for the work-item preview, and the live loop flips between them on every refresh:

- **Path A — metadata panel, resolved:** `formatMetadataPanel(..., metaBlockedBy)` renders one `Blocked By` row per active blocker. `metaBlockedBy` is produced by `resolveMetaBlockers()` (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`), which resolves asynchronously via `fetchBlockersForItem()` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`; spawns `wl dep list <id> --json` plus one `wl show` per candidate blocker) and caches the result in an in-memory `blockerCache` keyed by item ID.
- **Path B — metadata panel, unresolved:** until the lookup lands (or after the cache is dropped), `resolveMetaBlockers()` returns `undefined`, `state.metaBlockedBy` is `null`, and the panel renders **without** the `Blocked By` rows. A follow-up `render()` is scheduled from the fetch's `.finally()`, so the line pops in ~one lookup latency later (~0.5–2 s for two spawned `wl` processes).

**Why it repeats endlessly:** `doRefresh()` calls `blockerCache.clear()` on **every** list refresh (`worklist.ts`, in the refresh path). Every cache clear re-introduces the unresolved frame for the full async lookup, then the `.finally(render())` flips it back. Refreshes fire far more often than the 30 s tick in a live workspace:

- the DB-change watch (`db-change.ts`) reacts within ~150 ms (debounce) to any `wl` state-counter bump — real agent writes, and *every successful auto-sync* (`src/commands/sync.ts` bumps the read-cache counter) — each feeding `requestWatchRefresh → doRefresh`;
- the auto-sync task itself runs `doRefresh(false)` unconditionally on its cadence;
- `wl next` re-sorts bump the counter when the dispatcher runs it (`src/commands/next.ts`).

So under sustained write/sync traffic the line alternates on/off continuously — the reported "for a moment… disappear for a moment… repeat endlessly". The design intent ("an unresolved item renders without rows and a follow-up render shows them") assumed a one-time transition per selection; invalidating the cache on every refresh breaks that assumption.

**Secondary inconsistency (the "other path" the report refers to):** only the list-mode metadata panel renders `Blocked By`. The **detail view** (`formatDetailContent`, the other work-item preview render path) builds its metadata table from `buildMetaRows()` without blocker rows, and the hover tooltip (`formatTooltipLines`) also omits them — so the two preview render paths have already diverged (one has the line, the other does not).

## Users

- **Producer / operator** browsing the Herdr selection list. Story: "When I select a blocked item, I want the `Blocked By` line to appear once and stay put until the data actually changes — not flash on and off."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Selecting a dependency-blocked item shows the `Blocked By` line stably: once resolved, no render frame drops the line on subsequent auto-refresh ticks, DB-change (watcher) refreshes, or auto-sync cycles; observed over ≥3 consecutive refresh cycles with the DB otherwise idle.
- [ ] List refreshes never blank the panel: a refresh reuses the last known blockers for the same selected item (or resolves from the freshly fetched payload) instead of re-running the async lookup and rendering an unresolved frame; there is at most one spawn of `wl dep list` (and enrichment) per item until its edges can actually change (selection change, or a refresh that changed the item's dependency set).
- [ ] The live loop is bounded and self-terminating: a blocked item under simulated refresh + counter/watch events ends in a stable frame set (exactly one unresolved→resolved transition per selection), never an oscillating pair.
- [ ] Unblocked items are unaffected: their metadata panel output is byte-for-byte unchanged; headings, list navigation, description preview, and `m`/`M` scroll clamping (including `metadataPanelContentHeight` with `metaBlockedBy`) behave as before.
- [ ] The two preview render paths are reconciled: the detail view either renders the same `Blocked By` rows as the list metadata panel, or this divergence is explicitly documented out of scope with a code comment — but the report's "two paths, one has the line, one does not" inconsistency must be resolved one way or the other.
- [ ] Fail-open behaviour is preserved: a failed `wl dep list`/`wl show` still yields no `Blocked By` rows and never breaks rendering or navigation.
- [ ] Regression tests cover: stable frames across repeated refreshes for a blocked selection; single-flight/no re-spawn for an unchanged selection; cache reuse semantics; and the detail-view parity decision.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list. It is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Display-only change**: the fix must not create or mutate dependency edges, and must not change list-data shape for non-panel consumers.
- **Render path must never block**: keep synchronous rendering; any resolution stays async but never causes a visual regression to an earlier frame.
- **Reuse existing helpers**: `isActiveBlocker()` (`packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts`) and `parseDepListBlockersOutput()` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`).
- **No extra `wl` spawns on refresh**: refresh must not re-run the per-item blocker lookup when nothing about that item's edges changed.
- **Scope**: primary fix is the selection-list metadata panel flicker. Detail-view/tooltip parity is secondary and decided within this item (fix or explicitly documented out of scope).

## Existing state

- `resolveMetaBlockers` + `blockerCache`/`blockerInFlight` (async, per-selection, cached by item ID, cleared in `doRefresh`) — introduced by WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8.
- `formatMetadataPanel`/`buildMetadataPanelLines` render `Blocked By` rows from the `blockedBy` argument; `metadataPanelContentHeight` shares the same content so the scroll clamp matches the renderer (WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8).
- The DB-change watch (`db-change.ts`) deliberately watches only the state-counter file to avoid the WAL/`-shm` self-sustaining loop (WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN); the counter is bumped by every `wl` write, successful `wl sync`, and `wl next` re-sort byproduct (`src/read-cache-cli.ts`, `src/commands/sync.ts`, `src/commands/next.ts`) — the refresh triggers that drive the flicker cadence.
- Loop-free refresh machinery (single-flight + trailing coalescing in `doRefresh`, debounced `requestWatchRefresh`, scheduler at `scheduler.ts`) is in place and must be preserved.

## Desired change

Make the `Blocked By` state transition idempotent and non-regressive per selection:

1. Keep the renderer's two states (with/without rows) but stop re-clearing the cache on unrelated refreshes — invalidate only when the selected item's dependency edges can have changed (new selection, or a refresh that changes the item), or resolve blockers from the fresh payload so the resolved state survives refresh atomically.
2. Cache the in-flight lookup itself so repeated refreshes never race/duplicate the spawn, and re-render from cache thereafter.
3. Decide and implement detail-view parity (render the same rows or document the divergence).

## Key Files:

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `resolveMetaBlockers`, `blockerCache.clear()` in `doRefresh`, render-loop wiring of `metaBlockedBy`; `formatDetailContent`/`formatTooltipLines` for parity.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `fetchBlockersForItem` (lookup + per-edge enrichment); consider promise-level memoisation.
- `packages/herdr/src/db-change.ts`, `src/read-cache-cli.ts`, `src/commands/sync.ts`, `src/commands/next.ts` — the refresh triggers whose counter bumps set the flicker cadence (context; not expected to change).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-blockers.test.ts` — regression tests.

## Related work

- WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8 — "Show what an item is blocked on": parent feature that introduced the flickering async render path (regression source).
- WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN — "…DB-change watch" producer-rejection fix: the loop-free state-counter contract any fix must respect.
- WL-0MSGAEC5N006W5QA / WL-0MSGAEJQA005QG3W — read-cache + sync-heartbeat work that bumps the counter on sync (refresh frequency context).
- WL-0MSBVBNGH002RDP5 — prior "momentary collapse on refresh (flicker)" bug: the refresh path must stay atomic.
- WL-0MT9ZJF28004UJ28 — description-preview caching in the same metadata panel (precedent for cache-invalidation semantics).

### Related work (automated report)

- **WL-0MQP303A900780R0** – Escape key in Pi TUI work item detail view should navigate back to selection list (completed)
- **WL-0MT1JH1HN004JP1F** – T5: Metadata panel group info on heading (completed)
- **WL-0MQEJ2SLX009X17O** – Add risk and effort T-shirt size icons to Pi TUI work item selection list (completed)

Repository file matches: `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` (keyword overlap only).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the reported flicker is the list-mode metadata panel alternating between the unresolved and resolved `Blocked By` frames on repeated refreshes; the "two paths" wording also matches the detail view missing the line. Both readings are covered in the ACs.
- **Assumption:** refreshes in the reporter's environment were frequent enough (live workspace with agent writes / auto-sync / dispatcher `wl next`) to make the per-refresh blanking look continuous. The fix must be robust even under a fast refresh loop.
- **Risk — over-invalidation fix:** caching forever can show stale blockers after a real dependency change; the invalidation rule must distinguish "nothing changed" (reuse) from "item changed" (re-resolve).
- **Risk — spawn amplification:** the current code already spawns `wl dep list` + up to N× `wl show` per lookup; the fix must not add spawns to the refresh path.
- **Scope-creep risk:** detail-view/tooltip parity is tempting to expand; keep it to fix-or-document per AC5. Extra ideas should be tracked as separate work items, not scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required — the seed report plus repository investigation were sufficient to define the problem and the measurable acceptance criteria.

- Q (implicit): "Which code path renders the `Blocked By` line, and why does it flicker?" — Answer (investigation): two live states in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `resolveMetaBlockers()` returns `undefined` while the async `fetchBlockersForItem()` lookup is pending (line absent) and the cached array once it lands (line present); `doRefresh()` clears `blockerCache` on every refresh, so each refresh re-enters the absent state. Source: `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (`resolveMetaBlockers`, `blockerCache.clear()` in `doRefresh`) and `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` (`fetchBlockersForItem`).
- Q (implicit): "Do the two preview render paths differ?" — Answer (investigation): yes — list-mode `formatMetadataPanel` renders `Blocked By`; the detail view `formatDetailContent` (and the hover tooltip `formatTooltipLines`) build metadata from `buildMetaRows()` only and omit it. Source: `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`.
- Q (implicit): "What sets the flicker cadence?" — Answer (investigation + empirical check): the DB-change watch/react + auto-sync (successful `wl sync` bumps the read-cache state counter) + `wl next` re-sort byproduct bumps; verified with `wl list`/`wl show`/`wl dep list --json` that plain reads do not bump the counter. Source: `packages/herdr/src/db-change.ts`, `src/read-cache-cli.ts`, `src/commands/sync.ts`, `src/commands/next.ts`.

# Intake Brief — Restore `needsProducerReview` flag and producer-review icon in herdr selection list (WL-0MVAMS4RO000H3B0)

## Problem Statement

The `needsProducerReview` flag — the mechanism that marks a work item as awaiting Producer sign-off and drives the release gate — was removed from the database, CLI/API and herdr UI by WL-0MV85WFYU0071YQ9 + WL-0MV85WGIT004PHRC (children of epic WL-0MV82CHGQ000HAZZ), along with the producer-review icon ❌/✅ that used to appear in the herdr selection-list row prefix. The operator states this removal **should never have been created and implemented** — it was a misunderstanding somewhere along the line. The visible symptom was reported as a bug: *"The icon indicating the producer review status is no longer visible in the selection list in herdr."* The producer hold was re-homed onto the `assignee` field (`wl update <id> --assignee Map`), which is only surfaced through review-queue ordering — no icon, no at-a-glance signal, and no flag on the work item. This item restores the flag and its selection-list icon to the pre-removal behaviour, and an RCA child (WL-0MVAOYBZM0065AEN) traces how the wrongful removal item came to be created.

## Users

- **Producer / operator** scanning the herdr selection list to see which items await their review.
  - *As the producer, I want the list to show which items are awaiting my review (❌) and which have been reviewed (✅) at a glance, so I don't have to open every item or memorise assignee quirks.*
- **Downstream consumers of the flag** (release gate, audit runner, heartbeat, downtime dispatcher).
  - *As the release pipeline, I want `needsProducerReview` to gate the ship again, so unreviewed work cannot be released while the operator still expects that guarantee.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **DB restored:** a new migration re-adds the `needsProducerReview` column (kept idempotent; the shipped `20261015-drop-…` migration is neutralised as a metadata-sentinel no-op, mirroring how `20260210-add-…` was preserved); the field is back on `WorkItem`/query/input types, `VALID_FIELDS`, JSONL transport and both persistent-store schemas/row mappings, pinned by the restored migration/round-trip tests.
2. **CLI/API restored:** `wl reviewed` returns (with help entry + completion); `--needs-producer-review` is accepted by `wl create`/`wl update` and as a filter on `wl list`/`wl search`/`wl next`; the `api.ts` query param and `cli-types` surface are restored. Verified by restoring `tests/cli/reviewed.test.ts` and `tests/api-needs-producer-review-filter.test.ts`-style coverage.
3. **Selection-list icon visible again:** `getIconPrefixParts` in `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` renders the producer-review column (❌ `[REVIEW]` when true, ✅ `[OK]` when false, for all stages; empty when unset) exactly as at `e0f04202^`; `noIcons`/`WL_NO_ICONS` fallbacks work; a regression test asserts a flag-true item's list row contains the icon and a flag-false item's row shows the "done" state.
4. **herdr wiring restored:** the 6-bucket `in_review` grouping predicate returns (bucket 1 = `needsProducerReview === true`); fetcher/downtime-worker `select*`/`classifyItemForDispatch` exclude flag-true items from auto-dispatch again; `index.ts`, pane-lifecycle, pane-close*, stalled-work, settings and `worklist.ts` carry/use the flag; the metadata panel row and help-screen icon legend are restored and the legend drift guard passes.
5. **Theme/interview/shortcuts restored:** `src/theme.ts` producer-review icon helpers return; `src/commands/interview.ts` flag explain/clear flow returns; `src/commands/grouping.ts` + `helpers.ts` stop branching on the assignee for review semantics; the `r p` shortcut (shortcuts.json) acts on `needsProducerReview` again.
6. **Release/dispatch semantics restored (cross-repo, tracked as SA items):** `skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js` blocks release on `needsProducerReview === true` and the audit runner (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`) sets the flag on 'yes' verdicts — implemented via SorraAgents work items, not edited from this repo.
7. **Docs updated:** `docs/icons-design.md` (§3b restored with the icon column), `CLI.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` describe the flag again; the interview skill's `wl reviewed` handoff reference in the shared contract becomes valid again once the command is restored.
8. **RCA delivered:** the RCA child WL-0MVAOYBZM0065AEN reaches a terminal stage with a written root-cause chain and 3–5 concrete process recommendations.
9. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline. No CI/CD pipeline tests included.

## Constraints

- **Restore, don't redesign:** behaviour must match the pre-removal state (`e0f04202^` / `d18ea50d^`); do not invent a new icon scheme or flag semantics.
- **Migration history preserved:** never rewrite a shipped migration; add a new add-column migration and neutralise the shipped drop-migration (the established `20260210-add`/metadata-sentinel pattern).
- **Repo boundary:** `skill/` (SorraAgents) and `.pi/` files are not edited from this repo except the in-repo `.pi/skills/heartbeat` + `skill/pane-triage`-adjacent changes already made there; SA-side restore is tracked as SA work items linked from here.
- **Do not regress the legitimate audit-tier fix:** the status-neutral assignee-CAS claim and `--if-assignee` (WL-0MV7W77AY005MGBL fix within the epic) stay unless the RCA recommends otherwise — the flag's return must not reintroduce the `in-progress`/`in_review` hybrid claim bug.
- **UK English, Markdown descriptions, wl is source of truth**, push only to `dev`, build → test → commit order.
- **Sequencing:** the operator directed "restore … and then RCA" — the restore is the urgent (critical) deliverable; the RCA child follows/parallel and must not block the restore.

## Existing State

- Column dropped (`20261015-drop-needsProducerReview`); `wl reviewed` deleted (src/commands/reviewed.ts removed) and unregistered from CLI/help/completion; `--needs-producer-review` gone from create/update and list/search/next; api.ts param and cli-types removed; JSONL/type surface removed.
- Producer-review icon helpers, legend entries and the icon-prefix column removed from `packages/shared/src/icons.ts`; `src/theme.ts` helpers removed; `in_review` grouping collapsed to 5 buckets with bucket 1 = non-empty assignee (`inReviewBucket` in `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`).
- herdr: `producer-hold.ts` sentinel (`PRODUCER_HOLD_ASSIGNEE = 'Map'`, `isProducerHold`); `markProducerHoldWorkItem` writes `--assignee Map`; `r p` shortcut = `wl update <id> --assignee Map`; worklist prefix has no producer column; metadata panel has no producer row; `docs/icons-design.md` §3b documents "no dedicated icon column".
- Interview `wl reviewed` handoff in the shared skill contract refers to a command that no longer exists.
- Prior flag semantics (pre-removal): column default 0/false; `wl reviewed`; create/update `--needs-producer-review`; list/search/next filters; icon ❌/✅ for all stages; grouping bucket 1; ship gate + audit runner consumed it.

## Desired Change

1. Restore the flag end-to-end (column → types → CLI/API → herdr → theme → interview → docs → tests) to the pre-removal behaviour.
2. Restore the producer-review icon column in the herdr selection-list prefix (❌ `[REVIEW]` / ✅ `[OK]`), legend + metadata parity.
3. Restore dispatch/release semantics keyed on the flag (auto-dispatch exclusion, ship gate, audit runner 'yes' verdict).
4. Decide coexistence: keep the assignee-hold scheduling machinery (status-neutral audit claim, `r p` assignee write) alongside the restored flag, converting held items to flag=true on restore (open question — see Appendix Q2).
5. Deliver the RCA of how WL-0MV85WGIT004PHRC came to exist (child).

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — restore `needsProducerReviewIcon` (❌/✅ + `[REVIEW]`/`[OK]`), `ICON_LEGEND` entries, `iconLegendGlyphs`, and the icon-prefix column in `getIconPrefixParts` (`COLUMN 3`, pre-`e0f04202` shape).
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` + `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` + `src/persistent-store.ts` + `src/jsonl.ts` — column, schemas, row mappings, `VALID_FIELDS`, types.
- `src/migrations/index.ts` — new add-column migration; neutralise the shipped drop-migration.
- `src/commands/reviewed.ts` — recreate (from `e0f04202^`).
- `src/commands/{create,update,list,search,next}.ts`, `src/api.ts`, `src/cli-types.ts` — options/filters/query param/completion.
- `src/theme.ts`, `src/commands/grouping.ts`, `src/commands/helpers.ts`, `src/commands/interview.ts` — icon helpers, grouping, flag explain/clear.
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — 6-bucket predicate (bucket 1 = flag).
- `packages/herdr/src/{fetcher,downtime-worker,index,pane-lifecycle,pane-close*,stalled-work,settings,worklist}.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json`, `packages/herdr/src/producer-hold.ts` — flag wiring; `r p` action; icon+metadata render.
- `skill/heartbeat`, `.pi/skills/heartbeat`, `skill/pane-triage` — restore references (respecting repo boundary).
- Docs: `docs/icons-design.md`, `CLI.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/design/incremental-sync.md`.
- Tests: restore `tests/cli/reviewed.test.ts`, `tests/api-needs-producer-review-filter.test.ts`, `tests/herdr/icons.test.ts`, `tests/grouping-utility.test.ts`, `tests/migrations.test.ts`, `tests/unit/icons.test.ts`, `tests/cli/interview.test.ts` coverage; new regression test for the list-row icon.
- SA (tracked as SA items): `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, `skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js` + `check-audit-gate.js` + `run-release.js`, `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`.

## Related Work

- **WL-0MV85WGIT004PHRC** — the wrongful removal ("Remove needsProducerReview from herdr, theme and interview"); this item is its corrective counterpart (reverse).
- **WL-0MV85WFYU0071YQ9** — "Remove needsProducerReview from the worklog core" (DB/CLI removal being reversed).
- **WL-0MV82CHGQ000HAZZ** — parent epic "Option A … remove needsProducerReview"; its approach is the subject of the RCA.
- **WL-0MRJ3TUPP002TSGI** — original "reuse audit column for requiresProducerReview flag" icon design (the icon's lineage).
- **WL-0MV7W77AY005MGBL** — the root-cause bug the epic set out to fix (status-neutral audit claim must not be regressed while restoring the flag).
- **WL-0MVAOYBZM0065AEN** — RCA child of this item (created during this intake).
- **WL-0MSN6ZCTN0027U2R** — "flipping needsProducerReview must not make a valid audit stale" (freshness guarantee to re-pin).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **R1 — Partial restore leaves a hybrid:** restoring the flag while keeping assignee-based dispatch could double-gate held items. Assumption: both hold (belt-and-braces), with held items converted to flag=true; RCA may refine. Mitigation: decided explicitly in Appendix Q2 during planning.
- **R2 — Cross-repo SA work missing:** ship gate / audit runner restore must land via SA items or the release guarantee stays assignee-only. Mitigation: SA items created during planning (linked children).
- **R3 — Restoring a dropped column carries drifty states:** 698+ items were re-assigned/cleared by the legacy cleanup (WL-0MV85WFDS0036INQ); on restore the flag defaults false. Mitigation: flag semantics documented; any items still `assignee=Map` get flag=true via the same migration/script.
- **R4 — Re-introducing the hybrid claim bug:** naive revert of the epic's claim path would resurrect `in-progress`/`in_review` coercion (WL-0MV7W77AY005MGBL). Mitigation: keep the status-neutral assignee CAS claim; restore only the flag surface around it.
- **R5 — Scope creep:** converting every epic remnant (e.g. sync regression-guard behaviour for `assignee`) is a separate concern; keep this item to the flag + icon + gate semantics. Extra opportunities recorded as linked items, not scope.
- **Assumption:** "restore the pre-removal state" is judged from `e0f04202^` / `d18ea50d^` (the commits before the removals), not from further history.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (round 1, superseded): "What should the producer indicator reflect / look like / where appear?" (three multiple-choice questions proposing assignee-derived designs) — Answer (operator, 2026-10-16): **"No, No, No, No. WL-0MV85WGIT004PHRC should not have been created and implemented. That is a misunderstanding somewhere along the line. Restore the needsProducerReview flag and icon and then RCA how that item was created."** → The agent's assignee-derived framing was rejected; the deliverable is the **restoration of the removed flag + icon**, plus an RCA of the removal item's creation. Source: interactive reply. Evidence: removal commits e0f04202 / d18ea50d; removed surface enumerated from `git show`.
- Q2 (OPEN QUESTION during planning): do the assignee-hold features introduced alongside the removal (status-neutral CAS claim, `--if-assignee`, `r p` assignee write, sync `assignee` un-guarding) stay? **Recommended:** keep the dispatch/claim fix (R4), restore the flag as the reviewer signal, and convert surviving `assignee=Map` holds to `needsProducerReview=true` (R3). Operator may overrule.
- Note: the interview contract's `wl reviewed <id> true` producer-review handoff is currently broken (command removed); restoring `wl reviewed` (AC2) re-validates that contract.

## Effort and Risk (sizing)

- Effort: **Large** — full-stack reversal across DB/CLI/herdr/theme/interview/docs/tests plus SA-side coordination (see WL-0MV82CHGQ000HAZZ's Large sizing for the analogous removal).
- Risk: **High** — touches release gating, DB migrations and dispatch; mitigations in Risks & Assumptions; the wrongful-removal RCA guards against repetition.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MV85WESL002SD0F** – Ship release gate re-homed onto the assignee hold (completed)
- **WL-0MV85WGIT004PHRC** – Remove needsProducerReview from herdr, theme and interview (completed)
- **WL-0MT2GITCX009WUEW** – Remove packages/herdr/src/icons.ts and rewire herdr consumers (completed)

---

## Plan (decomposition)

Planning performed with the plan skill; pre-check returned **plan** (Large / Severe). Approval gate returned `request_approval=false` (Large, not Extra Large). Answers: **Q1=A** full restore, **Q2=C** keep the status-neutral audit-claim fix and revert the producer-review re-homing, **Q3=A** convert surviving holds.

### Features (children)

| # | Work item | Feature | Type | Priority | Depends on |
|---|-----------|---------|------|----------|-----------|
| F1 | WL-0MVAPEZBO005OZVH | Test-first: restore producer-review regression suite & icon contract | task | high | — |
| F2 | WL-0MVAPEZTE005T27J | Tracer bullet: `needsProducerReview` flag round-trip + selection-list icon | feature | high | F1 |
| F3 | WL-0MVAPF0AD006WHE4 | Complete CLI/API surface: `wl reviewed`, filters, api, completion | feature | high | F1, F2 |
| F4 | WL-0MVAPF0RN002F51Z | herdr dispatch & grouping restore | feature | high | F1, F2 |
| F5 | WL-0MVAPF19Q0096EP0 | Theme/interview/shortcuts restore + producer-hold retirement | feature | high | F1, F2, F3 |
